messages:
maya_sales: ACME POC kickoff. They want a Python WebSocket demo that: realtime streaming, supports function/tool calls (search + enrich), outputs strict JSON matching their schema, and notes on KMS/BYOK for logs. They also asked about SAML SSO for access control and a pricing ballpark for bursts (5k concurrent, ~45s/session, ~200 tokens output). Can we drop a concise backend handshake + websocket proxy sample and short answers for SAML/KMS?

jess_devex: I can do a tiny example. Backend -> Redwood proxy is safest (no browser API keys). Minimal Python (websockets + requests):

```py
# backend proxy (Flask + websockets pseudo)
import requests, json, asyncio, websockets

# 1) create ephemeral token from Redwood
h = requests.post('https://api.redwood.com/v1/handshake', json={
  'client_id': 'acme-poc', 'allowed_origin': 'https://app.acme.com'
})
token = h.json().get('token')
stream_url = 'wss://api.redwood.com/v1/streams?model=redwood-stream-small'

async def forward(ws_from_client):
    # open ws to Redwood with ephemeral token
    async with websockets.connect(stream_url, extra_headers={'Authorization': f'Bearer {token}'}) as ws_red:
        # forward messages both ways
        async for msg in ws_from_client:
            await ws_red.send(msg)
        # receive and forward
        async for chunk in ws_red:
            await ws_from_client.send(chunk)
```

jess_devex: On the browser side, the app connects to your backend WS endpoint (no Redwood key in-browser). For structured output include an output_schema in the initial request body and set `strict_parsing: true`. The stream will emit newline-delimited JSON chunks. Example structured chunk: `{"type":"structured_chunk","items":[{"id":"123","title":"x","confidence":0.92}]}`.

sam_soleng: Function/tool call flow: model can emit `{"type":"tool_call","tool":"search","args":{"q":"error 500"}}`. Your backend should detect these and run your internal search, then POST the result back to Redwood via server-to-server endpoint `/v1/streams/{stream_id}/tool_result` with the tool output. For websockets the stream_id is included in the handshake chunk.

sam_soleng: Also note: we support two modes for tool results: (1) immediate server response via the websocket proxy, or (2) async server POST if the tool work is heavy. The SDK supports `on('tool_call')` handler that simplifies that.

rachel_pricing: Quick pricing ballpark (hosted): assume $0.00035 per token output, input tokens similar magnitude. 200 output tokens = $0.07/session. 5k concurrent * $0.07 = $350 per concurrent-minute. Sessions ~45s -> roughly $263 per peak minute before input tokens and overhead. Add 15% buffer -> ~$302/minute. If they want guaranteed capacity look at Dedicated reserved bundles (flat commit + lower per-token). I can produce a 3-tier estimate (hosted burst, reserved monthly, reserved annual) if they want.

tom_infra: SAML/Security notes: for POC we usually do one of: (A) demo accounts (fast), (B) OAuth service-account tokens scoped to the POC, or (C) short SAML integration via our SSO team (more work). IP allowlist for direct egress (if they want Redwood's ingest restricted) is available for Dedicated/Private. For browser flows the recommended pattern is backend handshake to get ephemeral token; this avoids issuing long-lived creds to browser.

aditi_sec: Short answers for compliance questionnaire (pasteable):
- SOC2: Redwood maintains SOC2 Type II for hosted; report available under NDA.
- KMS/BYOK: Hosted uses cloud-managed keys by default. Dedicated and Private allow customer-managed KMS (BYOK/HSM) and encryption-at-rest options.
- Data residency: Private deployments can be deployed to customer VPC/region; hosted offers region selection for data residency.
- Audit & logs: per-request audit logs available; retention configurable under enterprise contracts.
- SAML/SSO: We integrate with IdPs via SAML/OIDC for enterprise work; POCs can use scoped ephemeral tokens.

aditi_sec: One-liner for RFP: "Private deployment supports VPC-only control plane, customer-managed KMS/HSM, audit logs, and enterprise SLAs; hosted plans include SOC2 compliance and region selection."

maya_sales: ACME also wants assurance on schema strictness: their UI will break if extra fields appear. Can we guarantee exact fields only?

jess_devex: You can enforce strict schema by sending `output_schema` + `strict_parsing: true`. We try to coerce model output to schema. For absolute guarantee: validate on backend and drop/transform extra fields before returning to UI. We also support `parse_mode: json_strict` which triggers an additional post-processing parse step and a `schema_violation` metric in the response.

sam_soleng: Practical pitfall: streaming emits partial chunks; don't feed partial JSON to UI. Buffer until you receive `{"type":"final"}` or until the SDK's `onComplete` callback fires. The SDKs provide `on('structured', obj)` only when full object parsed.

tom_infra: Networking gotcha: if they plan to test from corporate network with strict proxies, ask for egress rules (TLS MITM) and we can provide test endpoints and certificate pins for the POC.

deploy-bot: Deploy succeeded: `presales/python-ws-proxy` -> commit a1b2c3 on branch `presales-ws-demo` (staging).
